name: minerva-production-01 training layouts, 2026-10-18
use: Training-data generation only: python -m robot_platform.evaluation generate --workcell config/devices/simulation/minerva-production-01-workcell.json --randomize <this file>. Each attempt draws its own layout from these ranges (simulation.layouts); the workcell file stays the fixed layout. None of these is a measurement: each is a training-randomization design choice, centred where the head camera's depth put the real box and blocks (docs/development/SIM_WORKCELL.md, "The head camera's depth"); re-centre them when the box and blocks are taped and weighed.
frame: Regions are in the robot's base frame (urdf/minerva, metres: x toward the robot's left, y backward, the robot faces -y) with the table group where the workcell file puts it; the drawn table offset then moves the table, the tags and the head camera calibrated against them, the bucket and the block together. A block's length is along its yaw, its width across, its height up; a bucket's inside length is along its own y axis (front to back before its yaw), its width across.

length.source: training randomization, design choice 2026-10-18 (the coordinator, re-centred on the depth check): uniform 30-55 mm, each edge drawn on its own so the blocks are cuboids; centred on 42.5 mm, around the head camera's fits of the two real blocks (about 37 x 52 mm and 47 x 48 mm across, +/-4 mm; docs/development/SIM_WORKCELL.md, "The head camera's depth") and the user's 38.1 mm (1.5 in)

width.source: training randomization, design choice 2026-10-18 (the coordinator, re-centred on the depth check): uniform 30-55 mm, each edge drawn on its own so the blocks are cuboids; centred on 42.5 mm, around the head camera's fits of the two real blocks (about 37 x 52 mm and 47 x 48 mm across, +/-4 mm; docs/development/SIM_WORKCELL.md, "The head camera's depth") and the user's 38.1 mm (1.5 in)

height.source: training randomization, design choice 2026-10-18 (the coordinator, re-centred on the depth check; raised to 35 mm, accepted by the user): uniform 35-55 mm, centred on 45 mm, around the real blocks' tops at 37.0 and 39.0 mm above the table (the head camera's depth; docs/development/SIM_WORKCELL.md, "The head camera's depth"). Under about 35 mm the demonstrator's left, backing out of the handoff, passes within 1 mm of the right's fingers (a planner follow-up; docs/development/SIM_DEMONSTRATOR.md, "Blocks that are not cubes")

mass.source: placeholder: the workcell's cube mass per volume (its placeholder 35 g for the 38.1 mm cube) times the drawn block's volume; no block has been weighed

yaw_deg.source: training randomization, design choice 2026-10-18: uniform, centred on 0 (square to the table); a cuboid looks the same every half turn, so this covers every yaw (the depth fits turned the real blocks -37 and -22 degrees)

region.source: training randomization, design choice 2026-10-18: anywhere in the reachable work area, centred on the left arm's reach on the table: where the left picks a 38.1 mm cube (yaws 0 and 45 degrees) and hands it over with every move clear by over 1 mm, the bucket out of the way, on the interim layout (6 cm map, 2026-10-18; docs/development/SIM_GENERATION.md, "Randomized layouts"). Base frame, the table group where the workcell puts it

inner_width.source: training randomization, design choice 2026-10-18 (the coordinator, re-centred on the depth check): uniform 130-200 mm inside across, centred on 165 mm, around the head camera's depth's 155 mm (docs/development/SIM_WORKCELL.md, "The head camera's depth"; the user's 6 in, 152 mm)

inner_length.source: training randomization, design choice 2026-10-18 (the coordinator, re-centred on the depth check): uniform 200-300 mm inside front to back, centred on 250 mm, around the head camera's depth's 242 mm (233 mm at the bottom to 252 mm at the rim with the front wall's lean; docs/development/SIM_WORKCELL.md, "The head camera's depth")

height.source: training randomization, design choice 2026-10-18 (the coordinator, re-centred on the depth check): uniform 150-220 mm walls, centred on 185 mm, around the head camera's depth's rim at 189 mm (docs/development/SIM_WORKCELL.md, "The head camera's depth")

yaw_deg.source: training randomization, design choice 2026-10-18 (the coordinator, re-centred on the depth check): uniform within 30 degrees of -19.4, centred on the real box's turn from square to the tag rectangle as the head camera's depth measured it (docs/development/SIM_WORKCELL.md, "The head camera's depth")

region.source: training randomization, design choice 2026-10-18 (the coordinator, accepted by the user: kept to what the head camera sees): centred on the head camera's view of the drop-mapped region, which holds the depth-measured box's centre (-0.155, -0.587) m near its edge toward the robot's right. The part of the earlier region (x -0.45 to 0.075 m, y -0.47 to -0.85 m, where some drop plans and clears for the training sizes' corners) where a drawn bucket's whole opening stays in the head image most often and the demonstrator plans: in a 360-draw map with every draw planned (2026-10-18; docs/development/SIM_GENERATION.md, "Randomized layouts"), 68% of its buckets showed their opening with 5 px to spare and 67% planned. Right of x -0.17 m the opening leaves the image's right edge, beyond y -0.72 m its top edge, and nearer than y -0.57 m the bucket is in the way of the handoff. Base frame, the table group where the workcell puts it

cube_clearance.source: training randomization, design choice 2026-10-18: the bucket's outer walls at least 3 cm from the block's footprint (its circumscribed circle), so the left's approach has room; the planner checks the rest

x.source: training randomization, design choice 2026-10-18 (the coordinator widened the announced +/-3 cm): uniform +/-4 cm, centred on the interim robot-to-rectangle placement (fiducials.rectangle.robot_offsets), which nobody has measured

y.source: training randomization, design choice 2026-10-18 (the coordinator widened the announced +/-3 cm): uniform +/-4 cm, centred on the interim robot-to-rectangle placement (fiducials.rectangle.robot_offsets), which nobody has measured

yaw_deg.source: training randomization, design choice 2026-10-18 (announced to the user): uniform +/-3 degrees about the middle of the tag rectangle, centred on square to the robot (fiducials.rectangle.yaw_deg, not measured)

shift.source: training randomization, design choice 2026-10-18 (announced to the user): uniform +/-2 cm along each axis of the rectangle frame, centred on the depth-anchored pose (the head camera's depth and tags, frame depth-20261018T044530Z; docs/development/SIM_WORKCELL.md); the camera sits on a temporary mount

turn_deg.source: training randomization, design choice 2026-10-18 (announced to the user): uniform +/-2 degrees about each of the camera's own axes, centred on the depth-anchored pose (the head camera's depth and tags, frame depth-20261018T044530Z; docs/development/SIM_WORKCELL.md); the camera sits on a temporary mount

bucket_opening.source: training randomization, design choice 2026-10-18 (the coordinator, accepted by the user): every accepted layout's head image holds the bucket's whole opening (the four corners of its inside rim at the walls' top), with the layout's own drawn camera pose, each corner at least 5 px inside the recorded 320 x 240 image (10 px at the camera's 640 x 480; about 0.9 degrees). Centred on nothing: the margin is kept under the depth-measured box's own, which sits about 9 px from the image's right edge, so the real layout passes

position_draws.source: training randomization, design choice 2026-10-18: bucket positions drawn per layout until one is on the table and clear of the block; centred on nothing (a cap)

plan_draws.source: training randomization, design choice 2026-10-18: layouts drawn per attempt until the demonstrator plans one; centred on nothing (a cap). Every rejected draw is counted in the manifest and the episode's metadata
